Ardia product signal report

Public GitHub activity of mantrakp04/ardia · reports from 2026-09-29 to 2026-11-11 · data pulled 2026-11-11 · built 2026-11-11 09:34 UTC

Overview

A quick orientation: what this report covers, how to read it, and where to go next.

584threads (issues + discussions)
816evidence units
304unique people (246 users)
427problem clusters (146 with 2+ people)
How to read this
  • Evidence unit: one distinct problem an LLM extracted from a thread (a thread can yield several). Cluster: evidence units grouped by semantic similarity; the name and description are LLM-written. Only clusters with 2+ unique people are shown.
  • Unique people = thread/comment authors plus users who said they are also affected (maintainers and bots excluded). Users (u) never authored a PR in this repo; contributors (c) have. Shown as "N (Uu/Cc)".
  • Fix coverage: "k of n threads fixed" counts a cluster's threads that have a deterministic link (PR, commit, release note or maintainer comment) to a fix. Clusters often mix related-but-distinct bugs, so partial coverage is common.
  • Status: SHIPPED fixes linked for all threads, no confirmed recurrence · IN_PROGRESS open PR touching the remaining threads · PARTIALLY_ADDRESSED some fix, other threads still open · UNRESOLVED no fix or PR found · STILL_REPORTED_AFTER_FIX similar reports dated after a fix release · UNKNOWN too little evidence. Each cluster has a "Why this status" line.
  • Confidence: L1 links are deterministic GitHub references (high; medium when the release is inferred from a merge date). L3 links are an LLM judgement (0 to 1); those below 0.7 are shown but not used for status. LLM judgments are not ground truth.

Where to go

Key findings

Which patterns in user reports are clear enough to state plainly, with the evidence behind each?

These observations are hand-checked against the underlying threads. Each links to its evidence. They describe what users report and what shipped. They make no claim about what Ardia should prioritise. The repo is six weeks old (first issue Sep 29, most activity from Oct 22), so "rising" flags elsewhere in this report mean little: almost every group is new in the last 30 days.

1. Apple Passwords and iCloud Passwords: the largest group with no fix

5 threads, 11 people, Oct 22 → Oct 30. Users cannot fill logins or verification codes from Apple Passwords or the iCloud Passwords extension, and logins saved in Ardia cannot be used by Safari, other apps or macOS AutoFill.

Two threads were closed as not planned, #565 and #669. Three are still open:

  • #18 (Oct 22, iCloud Passwords extension not supported)
  • #350 (Oct 25, fill from the Passwords app)
  • #379 (Oct 25, an AutoFill credential provider so Ardia logins work elsewhere)

A neighbouring group, "Mac passkeys cannot be used to sign in" (3 people, #1060 still open), points the same way. Across the whole passwords and passkeys area (32 people), no problem group is fully shipped: 5 are partially addressed and 2 are unresolved.

2. Blank Google sign-in popups: 11 people, fixed within days

5 threads, 11 people, Oct 26 → Nov 7. "Sign in with Google" and other SSO popups opened blank and blocked login (#436, #582, #708, #964).

Fixes shipped in an engine build on Oct 28 and in v0.2.43 (Oct 31). The recurrence check judged four later similar reports to be different problems. #647 (a blank popup only when sign-in asks for new permissions) is still open. This group is as large as the passwords one, but it was handled quickly.

3. Users arrive from Arc and Dia, and ask for parity

94 of 816 problem reports (84 threads, 70 people) name Arc or Dia. Half are feature requests ("as in Arc"), and a third are bugs where Ardia behaves differently from Arc. Examples:

  • ⌘D should pin the tab as in Arc, not open the bookmark popup (#1134, open)
  • ⌥⌘←/→ should switch profiles, as in Dia and Arc (#1149, open)
  • Arc pinned folders were lost on import (#32, fixed); split and top-level pins are still missed (#1084, Nov 9, closed as completed)

The "Imported pins are duplicated, missing, or split" group has 7 people, and #487 (Zen import merges segmented profiles) is still open. Shortcut parity is one of the 9 groups reported again after a fix: ⌘D still opened the bookmark popup 17 days after the v0.2.40-nightly.9 fix (confidence 0.85).

4. Window chrome is the biggest area and holds most of the repeat reports

Windows and themes is the largest area: 92 problem reports from 59 people (window chrome, fullscreen, Little Ardia placement, macOS tiling, app icons). Five of the 9 groups reported again after a fix are in this area:

  • thin margins make the window hard to drag
  • the app icon ignores macOS tint and icon styles
  • window drags do not trigger macOS snapping
  • Little Ardia opens on the wrong display
  • external links open in the wrong space or profile

Each is small (2–3 people), but together they read as a run of macOS-integration edge cases that a first fix does not fully close.

5. One reporter accounts for most of the bookmarks threads

The "Bookmarks cannot stay open in a right sidebar" group has 14 threads but only 4 people. 11 of the 14 threads are from one reporter (e.g. #750, #818, #1071), often bundling several requests per issue. The report counts people, not threads, so this group ranks by its 4 people. A thread-count view of the tracker would overstate it. The underlying requests are real, though: a persistent right-side bookmarks panel, bookmark export, and a freeze with "Always show bookmark bar". The panel was reported again after the v0.2.44 fix (confidence 0.74).

6. Intel Macs: one open issue with 4 people since launch week

#67 "Intel build" (Oct 23) is still open, with 4 people reporting that the current release does not run on Intel Macs. It is the largest single-thread group with no fix or PR.

7. Responsiveness: a fix in about a day, 128 releases in seven weeks

Over 234 user-reported threads that were fixed, the median time to fix is 1.0 day (middle half 0.5–3.1 days). The median first maintainer reply is also about 1 day. The repo shipped 128 releases (stable, nightly and engine builds) between Sep 25 and Nov 10. The project has one maintainer, mantrakp04. Of 808 issues, 352 are closed as completed, 50 as not planned, and 378 are open.

How far to trust this:

  • Extraction used GPT-6.1 Sol via Codex for 547 threads and Grok 4.7 for the 53 newest. Taxonomy, naming, fix verification and recurrence checks used Grok 4.7. These are LLM judgements, not ground truth.
  • Grok flagged 82 of 146 problem groups as mixing several problems (the Graphify run with Sonnet flagged about 8%). Ardia's issues are narrow UI requests, so groups often bundle neighbouring requests. Read a group's member reports before quoting its name.

Top problems

What are users currently struggling with most, ranked by how many different people reported it?

Rising problems

Which problems are being reported by noticeably more people lately than before?

Method: unique people (authors + also-affected) in the last 30 days vs the previous 60 days (as a per-30-day rate), measured back from the newest evidence date. Flagged rising when the last 30 days have at least 3 people and at least twice the earlier rate. No forecasting.

Clusters

Themes (groups of related clusters, cut at a looser similarity)

Demand

Do 👍 reactions point to the same problems as the people counts do?

Reactions are an extra, noisy demand signal: one 👍 (issues) or upvote (discussions) on a thread's opening post, summed over a cluster's threads. They favour visible, older or well-shared threads and only some users react, so read them next to the people count, not instead of it. The 👍 column is also in the Top problems table and the All problems explorer.

Themes

What are the bigger topics that many individual problems fall under?

Themes group related clusters (the same clustering cut at a looser similarity). 209 themes; 109 are named (2+ people), the rest are single-person themes labelled with a representative problem. Click a row for its clusters; a cluster name opens it in Top problems. Status bar = share of the theme's clusters by status. Sorted by unique people by default.

All problems

Can I find a specific problem, including ones only a single person reported?

Every extracted problem (816), including 259 that sit in one-off clusters (a single problem, not repeated anywhere) and so are not in Top problems. Text search covers problem, context and requested solution. "Grouped" = the problem is in a cluster of 2+ problems. Status = status of the problem's cluster. Filters combine; 50 rows per page.

Shipped fixes

Which reported problems have a fix, and which release carried it?

Chain: problem (cluster) → report → PR / commit → release and date. Clusters with status SHIPPED, newest release first. "L1" = deterministic reference; "release inferred" = the first release published after the merge/commit rather than one named in a release note.

Unresolved problems

Which recurring problems have no fix, or only a partial one, so far?

Clusters with status UNRESOLVED, or PARTIALLY_ADDRESSED with fix coverage of 50% or less. Default order: unique people, then number of threads, recency, average severity. This lists evidence only; it says nothing about what should be built.

Reported after fix

Where did people keep reporting a problem after a fix release shipped?

A later report counts only if it is dated after the fix release, is from a different thread, is close in embedding space to the fixed report (cosine ≥ 0.82), and an LLM judged it the same problem or a regression. Possible interpretations, not chosen between: the fix was incomplete; a regression; a documentation / discoverability gap; or a different underlying issue that reads similarly.

Confirmed (LLM confidence ≥ 0.7)

Possible recurrence (0.5–0.69 confidence)

Lower-confidence verdicts, computed in this report only. Not counted in any status. Read as leads, not conclusions.

Areas

Which parts of the product draw the most user signal, and does engineering activity match it?

Areas are approximate LLM-assigned labels and activity counts are proxies (release-note bullets, shipped PRs, issues closed as completed; routed to areas by deterministic links where possible, otherwise by embedding similarity). Ratio = share of user signal divided by share of visible engineering activity; a descriptive comparison only.

Time to fix

Question: how long does a fix take? Time to first maintainer response

Contributors

Who actually writes the fixes: the reporters themselves, maintainers, or other outside contributors?

Descriptive only. Over threads opened by users or contributors (not maintainers or bots) whose fix is linked (status "fixed"), who authored the change that fixed it: self-fixed = the reporter authored the fixing PR or commit; maintainer = a maintainer authored the fix (and the reporter did not); contributor = another outside person did; unknown = no PR or commit author could be identified (e.g. a release-note-only link). Fixing PRs are those linked as primary or linked and merged or closed; the maintainer usually lands fixes as commits, and where a contributor PR and a maintainer commit are both linked the thread counts as maintainer.

Method & data

Where does the data come from, how was it processed, and what are the limits?

Data

The underlying data (derived fields only, no raw GitHub bodies) is in share/ (SQLite, CSV and JSON bundle) with the column-by-column description in docs/DATA_DICTIONARY.md. Both paths are relative to this file's location in the repo (output/), so they only work while the report sits alongside the repo; they are not embedded in this page.

Methodology

Data window. The sync fetches everything updated since 2026-04-01. The repository was created after that date, so this covers its full public history. User reports in the data run from 2026-09-29 to 2026-11-11. GitHub data was pulled on 2026-11-11.

Data flow

  1. Deterministic: GitHub API sync of issues, discussions, PRs, commits, releases and comments into SQLite; reference parsing (closes/fixes, closing-issue references, "fixed in" maintainer comments, commit references, release-note bullets); noise filtering; L1 fix resolution per thread; unique-user counting, coverage, trend and status rules.
  2. Embeddings (local model Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B-ST-local): clustering (run t0.20, average-linkage cosine distance 0.20), themes (looser cut 0.27), L2 candidate matches, area activity routing.
  3. LLM (GPT-6.1 Sol via Codex (most extraction) and Grok 4.7 via Cursor (remaining extraction, taxonomy, naming, verification, recurrence)): evidence extraction (extract-v3), area taxonomy, cluster/theme naming, L3 verification of candidate fixes, recurrence checks. The only LLM prose shown is the cluster name / description / distinction and the short reasons attached to L3 and recurrence verdicts.

Thresholds

  • L3 verdicts count toward status only at confidence ≥ 0.7; recurrence candidates need cosine ≥ 0.82; confirmed recurrence needs LLM confidence ≥ 0.7; the "possible" tier uses 0.5–0.69.
  • An open PR counts as IN_PROGRESS only if updated in the last 30 days. Rising = last-30-day people ≥ 3 and ≥ 2x the previous 60-day per-30-day rate.
  • Status counts (clusters with 2+ people): UNRESOLVED 23, SHIPPED 27, PARTIALLY_ADDRESSED 42, IN_PROGRESS 44, STILL_REPORTED_AFTER_FIX 9, UNKNOWN 1.

Limitations

  • Discord and other community chat are excluded by design; this is GitHub only.
  • Discussion comments are not parsed for fix links, so discussion threads rarely show a fix and read as "no fix signal".
  • Area labels are noisy; clusters can mix related-but-distinct problems (a warning icon marks clusters the naming step flagged as incoherent), which is why coverage is shown next to status.
  • LLM judgments (extraction, naming, L3 verification, recurrence) are not ground truth. Unique-people counts depend on extraction of "also affected" mentions.
  • Releases marked "inferred" are the first release after the merge or commit, not confirmed.
  • Many verified matches are "partially addresses": clusters usually contain several related bugs.
